outlooks.summary: Isolated to widely scattered severe thunderstorms remain possible Thursday from the Missouri Ozarks to the lower Ohio Valley and Tennessee Valleys as well as the northern High Plains and northern Rockies.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Upper trough currently extending along the West Coast will gradually progress eastward throughout the day, likely extending from southern British Columbia through the Great Basin by 12Z Friday. Ridging will build across the Plains with the increasingly confluent flow ahead of the upper trough contributing to a gradual strengthening of the mid-level flow ahead of it. Farther east, the remnants of Alberto will continue northward into central Ontario, eventually becoming absorbed into the shortwave trough moving gradually across Ontario and upper Great Lakes. At the surface, low currently over eastern MT will become more defined throughout the day. Lee troughing will extend southward from this low to another low over southeast CO. Convective outflow from the ongoing MCS across northern OK/southern KS is expected to extend from southern IL across southern MO and into northeast OK.

sections.title: Ozark Plateau into the Mid-MS, Lower OH, and TN Valleys
sections.text: Expectation is for the remnants/convectively induced vorticity from the ongoing MCS over northern OK/southern KS to move across central MO and into central IL from the early afternoon into the early evening. Outflow from this system will likely extend southwestward from southern IL across southern MO and into northeast OK. Both of these features (i.e. the vorticity maximum and outflow boundary) will act as stimuli for convection as the airmass destabilizes. Given the mesoscale nature of both of these features, some uncertainty exists regarding their actual location during the afternoon but consensus, both from the HREF members and NAM/GFS, places them near the areas described above. Airmass across the region will be quite moist with surface dewpoints in the upper 60s/low 70s and 100-mb mean mixing ratios near 15 to 16 g per kg. Strong diurnal heating is also anticipated, with temperatures in the upper 80s during the afternoon. Mid-level lapse rates aren't overly steep but the warm and very moist airmass still supports MLCAPE over 2500 J/kg. Additionally, some enhancement to the mid-level flow is possible as a result of the remnant MCS. Expectation is for initial discrete storms cap

sections.title: Northern Great Basin into the northern High Plains
sections.text: Thunderstorms are anticipated again today ahead of the slow-moving upper trough moving across the Pacific Northwest. Mid-level flow is expected to be slightly higher than Wednesday with modestly increased instability also anticipated. Overall environment appears favorable for multicells (and maybe an isolated supercells) capable of severe hail and strong wind gusts. A somewhat separate threat area exist across far eastern MT and adjacent western ND. In this area, modest moisture return will help support airmass destabilization with surface convergence along the northern periphery of the surface low providing the forcing for thunderstorm development. Vertical wind profiles that veer with height may result in a few storms organized enough to produce large hail and/or strong wind gusts. A tornado or two also appears possible, particularly if a storm is able to realize the enhanced vorticity over the frontal zone. ..Mosier/Wendt/Gleason.. 05/31/2018

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms, mainly offering wind and hail, are possible from the Missouri Ozarks to the lower Ohio Valley and Tennessee Valleys, as well as the northern High Plains and northern Rockies.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The mid/upper-level pattern features a high-amplitude trough over the Pacific Coast States, with embedded shortwave trough/vorticity max apparent in moisture-channel imagery over coastal north-central CA near the Bay Area. The synoptic trough is expected to progress eastward to the northern Rockies and Great Basin by 12Z, with the aforementioned embedded perturbation ejecting northeastward to northwestern UT and southeastern ID by about 00Z. Downstream ridging will prevail over the central/southern Plains states and northward to MB. An overnight MCS has led to a pronounced MCV -- evident in satellite and composited radar imagery -- over extreme eastern KS. Probably because the causative convective complex had been so consistently forecast in some form by various synoptic and convection-allowing models, and then the MCV became well-developed overnight in keeping with much of the guidance, the resulting perturbation likewise is uncharacteristically well-defined in a strong consensus of progs. sections.title: Ozarks to OH/TN Valleys
sections.text: Scattered to locally numerous thunderstorms are possible today into this evening, with relatively discrete convection offering the greatest hail risk. One or two clusters of convection should aggregate over the slight and enhanced categorical-risk areas by late afternoon or early evening, with increasing potential for forward propagation and an organized wind threat. That conceptual (as well as numerical in several cases) model still appears valid. For now the main change is to make some eastward adjustments based on prior/overnight MCS behavior/speed, and related cloud/precip trends now observed. Additional thunderstorms also should develop southwestward along the outflow boundary across the Ozarks region of MO/AR. Rich low-level moisture is forecast across the outlook area with surface dew points in the upper 60s to low 70s F and 15-16 g/kg mean-mixing ratios being rather common. That moisture, along with strong diurnal heating (away from extensive cloud/precip areas related to the old MCS) will contribute to the development of preconvective peak MLCAPE in the 1500-2500 J/kg range south and east of the outflow boundary. sections.title: Northern High Plains
sections.text: Multiple areas and episodes of strong-severe thunderstorms are possible today into this evening within a corridor from the Canadian border southwestward across portions of MD/MT and northwestern WY, and southeastern ID, with isolated severe potentially occurring as far southwest as northeastern NV. Given the strengthening of deep shear over the ID/MT corridor, with the approach of the mid/upper trough and the ejecting/embedded shortwave perturbation, both isolated supercells and clusters of outflow-dominant convection are possible especially from southeastern ID northeastward. Other areas of convection should develop over parts of central/southern MT and western ND, in zones of low-level convergence with steep deep-layer lapse rates and MLCAPE 1000-2000 J/kg, atop well-mixed subcloud layers. Although low-level flow generally is forecast to be weak, favorable buoyancy and effective shear should support organized severe potential in the form of both hail and gusts. Tornado potential appears more conditional across the northern Plains, but may exist for any supercells that can interact with a residual frontal zone. ..Edwards/Smith.. 05/31/2018

outlooks.summary: Clusters of severe thunderstorms, mainly capable of wind and hail, are possible from the Missouri Ozarks to the lower Ohio Valley and Tennessee Valleys, as well as the northern High Plains and northern Rockies.

sections.title: Ozarks into OH Valley
sections.text: Multiple clusters of severe storms are expected to affect this region today, with the first currently producing damaging winds over southeast IL. These storms are expected to track eastward across southern IN and northern KY through much of the day. Ref MCD #584 and WW #136 for more information. In the wake of the initial band of storms, visible satellite imagery shows rapid clearing across southern MO. This will result in strong heating, steepening low-level lapse rates, and destabilization across this region by early afternoon. 12z models are consistent in re-development of intense storms over this area as a weak shortwave trough moves into the region from KS. The initial storms will potentially be supercellular with the risk of very large hail and a tornado or two. Storms should slowly organize and grow upscale as outflows merge, with an eventual bowing complex producing damaging winds expected to move across the ENH area through the evening.

sections.title: Northern Great Basin into Northern Rockies
sections.text: An active thunderstorm day is expected today from northeast NV and eastern ID into much of MT. A large upper trough is moving across CA, with large scale lift and strong winds aloft spreading across the risk area. Strong heating is occurring this morning, with dewpoints in the 50s over most of this region. Present indications are that scattered fast-moving cells will form over the higher terrain throughout this region, and along a cold front moving into NV/ID. Multiple clusters of strong/severe storms may persist through the afternoon and evening. Large hail and damaging wind gusts will be the main threats. ..Hart/Leitman.. 05/31/2018

outlooks.summary: Additional strong thunderstorm activity, accompanied by a risk for severe wind and hail, is expected across parts of southern Missouri and northern Arkansas into the lower Ohio Valley and Tennessee Valleys, as well as the northern High Plains and northern Rockies, late this afternoon and evening.

sections.title: 20Z Outlook Update
sections.text: Adjustments to categorical and severe probabilistic lines have been made in a number of areas. This is mostly in an attempt to better account for latest trends in destabilization, and impacts of ongoing/preceding convection. Strongest instability (thermodynamic profiles characterized by steep mid-level lapse rates and large CAPE) remains present in a corridor along/south of a convectively generated or enhanced boundary across parts of southern Kentucky into southern Missouri, where a 40-50 kt westerly 500 mb jet streak is contributing to strong vertical shear. Perhaps aided mostly by forcing for ascent associated with lower/mid tropospheric warm advection, it appears that another organized mesoscale convective system could evolve and propagate east/southeastward late this afternoon and evening accompanied by a risk for potentially damaging wind gusts. Initial storm development may include isolated supercells with primarily a severe hail threat, but a tornado or two might not be out of the question. For more specific information concerning ongoing or imminent severe weather potential, please refer to the latest SPC mesoscale discussions and watches. ..Kerr.. 05/31/2018 .PREV DISCUSS

outlooks.summary: Severe hail and wind is expected across parts of southern Missouri and northern Arkansas into the lower Ohio Valley and Tennessee Valleys, as well as the northern High Plains and Rockies through evening.

sections.title: MT into ND
sections.text: Cooling aloft and lift associated with an upper trough will persist tonight, with a surface low shifting into the northern High Plains. Easterly low-level winds will maintain a relatively moist and unstable air mass across MT, northern WY and the western Dakotas, with a storm threat likely into the night from MT into ND as capping increases over southern areas. A few cells will be capable of large hail, with a damaging wind threat with a few bowing structures. For more information see mesoscale discussion 600 and 601. ..Jewell.. 06/01/2018

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Line of storms has recently intensified. Trends will be monitored for a possible watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar, satellite, and lightning trends all suggest that cluster of storms over southern IL has recently intensified and has accelerated in its eastward movement. Storm motion is now over 40 knots, and localized damaging winds have recently been reported. The air mass ahead of the storms is becoming increasingly unstable with dewpoints in the 70s and strong heating. Given the increasing organization of the cluster, a severe thunderstorm watch may needed soon. ..Hart.. 05/31/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Some gusty winds are possible with storm cluster moving east/southeast across eastern KY toward far western VA this afternoon. The overall threat appears marginal at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of storms in the Bluegrass region of eastern KY will continue to track east/southeast this afternoon. Deep layer shear across the region remains light, but continued destabilization and increasing DCAPE values will be adequate for some stronger wind gusts. LEX recently saw a peak gust to 35 kt and potential exists for some marginally severe gusts through the afternoon, especially if the cluster can become better organized. At this time, the overall threat appears marginal and a watch is not imminent. However, trends will be monitored into the afternoon hours for any increase in intensity/organization.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat is rapidly increasing across southern MO into northern AR. A watch will likely be needed soon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Extensive cumulus field has developed in the vicinity of an outflow boundary from overnight convection. As morning clouds have quickly cleared from the area, temperatures have rebounded into the upper 70s to low 80s early this afternoon. With continued heating, capping will continue to erode and further destabilization will allow for convective initiation in the next couple of hours along/just south of the I-44 corridor in southwest MO. Deep layer shear around 40-50 kt will support supercell storms initially. Additionally, mean mixing ration values around 15-16 g/kg indicate high quality moisture across the region. While low level shear is not overly impressive, any cell that can remain discrete and interact with the surface boundary will pose a tornado threat. Directional shear in the lowest 3km is modest, so storms likely will tend to become outflow dominant with time. As such, upscale growth into one or more bowing segments is anticipated. Steep midlevel lapse rates, in conjunction with rather straight, long hodographs will further support large hail production, some of which may be 2+ inches. Given the quickly recovering airmass, a watch may be needed soon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A damaging wind threat will continue across Severe Thunderstorm Watch 136 and persist downstream toward parts of northern KY and southwest OH. A downstream watch will be needed soon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The mature bow echo currently tracking east-northeast at around 45 kt across southern IN and northern KY will move out of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 136 by around 19z. A severe threat is expected to persist downstream into parts of northern KY and southwest OH and a new watch may be needed downstream. Moderate instability exists across parts of northern KY into southwest OH downstream of the current watch. However, some uncertainty exists, at least across northern KY, due to earlier cluster of storms across the Bluegrass region. These storms have resulted in a weak cold pool in the LEX to JKL vicinity and this may inhibit severe potential across parts of the area. Furthermore, deep layer shear is rather weak and lapse rates decrease with eastward extent. However, rich moisture across the region and temperatures warming into the mid to upper 80s will promote continued destabilization ahead of the approaching bow echo. Some threat for damaging wind and perhaps small hail likely will persist for several hours and move out of WW 136 into southwest OH/northern KY and a downstream watch will likely be needed soon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Trends for convection are increasing and one or more Severe Thunderstorm Watches will be likely be needed this afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Large scale lift is currently impinging on regions experiencing low-level moistening atop modestly steep lapse rates (6.5-7.5 C/km within a 1-6km layer). The inclusion of diurnal heating occurring between cloud breaks along with the available low-level moisture and steepening lapse rates are allowing MUCAPE values to exceed 1000 J/kg in some locations within the discussion area. Given effective bulk shear values of 40-50 kts across the region, updraft organization is possible with any cells that manage to develop. Relatively straight hodographs suggest that large hail and perhaps damaging wind gusts will be the primary severe threats. Latest high resolution guidance suggests that transient supercells and bowing segments will be the dominant modes of convection, with convective coverage increasing within the next few hours. As such, one or more severe thunderstorm watches will likely be needed sometime this afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few strong wind gusts and small hail will be possible across parts of east-central and northeast IN into far southern Lower MI and northwest OH this afternoon. A watch is not expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Rich boundary layer moisture is present across the MCD area, with dewpoints from the mid 60s to near 70 F noted in 18z surface observations. Strong heating of this moist airmass has resulted in moderate instability, with MUCAPE values near 2000 J/kg. Modest midlevel lapse rates around 6.5-7 C/km were evident in RAP forecast sounding and mesoanalysis data, with steeper low level lapse rates resulting in DCAPE values around 1000-1500 J/kg. As a result, isolated to widely scattered storms have developed. Deep layer shear is weak across the region and this should limit overall organization. However, degree of instability will result in brief intense updrafts capable of small hail. Light low level flow coupled with the steep low level lapse rates/higher DCAPE values will further support occasional strong wind gusts with the most intense cells. Given the transient and marginal nature of the threat, a watch is not expected.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated to scattered strong storms will continue through the afternoon. A few strong wind gusts are possible with these storms, but the overall threat will remain marginal the remainder of the afternoon and a watch is not expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Scattered thunderstorms will continue through the afternoon in a very moist and unstable environment. Temperatures have warmed into the mid 80s to low 90s F across the region with dewpoints generally in the low 70s F. As a result, MLCAPE values near 2000 J/kg were noted. Deep layer shear and midlevel lapse rates are lackluster and this will limit longevity/organization, but DCAPE values are approaching 1500 J/kg and some strong wind gusts will continue to be possible through the remainder of the afternoon. Given the lack of a more organized threat, a watch is not expected at this time. While severe threat in the short term is expected to remain marginal, some hi-res guidance suggests a more organized bowing line may migrate into parts of Middle Tennessee later tonight, mainly after 00z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated severe may be possible within the next few hours, with more widespread coverage possible later this afternoon and evening. A WW may be needed for portions of the area in the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Isolated convection has developed across the discussion area within the last few hours, amidst a warming/moistening boundary layer beneath steep mid-level lapse rates. With up to 1500-2000 J/kg MLCAPE and 30-40kt of effective bulk shear present, isolated incidents of large hail or damaging winds are possible with the more robust updrafts in the near term. Later this afternoon, more widespread convection may develop across the discussion area or move into the region from the west. Latest model guidance suggests that adequate effective bulk shear and buoyancy will remain in place across the area during the late afternoon/early evening hours. Later storms may also become capable of damaging winds and large hail. Given the uncertainty of timing for more widespread severe, a WW may be issued for parts of the discussion area pending more favorable convective trends.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong to severe wind gusts will continue across severe thunderstorm watch 136 for another hour or two. Severe threat should lessen to the east and south of the watch area.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The bow echo moving eastward across northern KY has produced severe gusts at SDF and FFT over the last hour. Additional thunderstorm clusters have developed southward into central KY, though are not exhibiting the fast forward propagation that original bowing segment possessed. The surging portions of the bow will continue eastward across the Bluegrass region. However, a relative minimum in instability exists across this region and points east due to earlier convection. Observed temperatures across this region have cooled into the upper 60s to low 70s and this should impede severe threat further east. In fact, latest 7km CAPPI shows decreasing reflectivity over the last hour or so. The cluster of storms further south in central KY may continue to pose a strong wind threat given steep low level lapse rates/higher DCAPE values. However, weak deep layer shear is likely limiting overall organization. ..Leitman.. 05/31/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated strong wind gusts will be possible, though the threat should be brief in both time and space. A watch is not expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The airmass across southeast KY into northeast TN and far western VA has remained relatively free of convection this afternoon. Currently, lines of convection are converging on this area, where a very moist, warm and unstable environment is in place. As storms develop/merge over the area, strong wind gusts will be possible. The overall threat should remain limited in space and time and a watch is not expected.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong wind gusts will continue to be the main threat across WW 137 the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong to severe gusts continue from just east of Cincinnati northward toward VES near the IN/OH state line. Latest radar loop from ILN indicates that outflow has surged ahead of cells across southwest OH and is now intersecting storms moving into west-central OH just to the west of VES. New cells could develop along the surging outflow and pose a strong wind threat into west-central OH. As such, Severe Thunderstorm Watch 137 has been extended northward. A damaging wind threat will continue across WFO ILNs area for a few more hours before waning with loss of daytime heating. With WW 137 set to expire at 22z, a local extension in time may be needed depending on convective trends. ..Leitman.. 05/31/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Multiple storm/boundary mergers will support a threat of isolated downburst winds and/or marginally severe hail through about 23z. The limited magnitude and duration of the threat suggest a watch is probably not necessary.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An outflow boundary is moving southward into south central and southeast KY with ongoing convection, and is beginning to merge with outflow from a separate cluster in northeast middle TN. A narrow corridor of surface heating and moderate buoyancy remains in the corridor where these boundaries will merger over the next 1-2 hours, to the northwest of rain-cooled air across the southern Appalachians. Vertical shear is weak over the area of the boundary mergers, but low-midlevel lapse rates are sufficiently steep to support strong updrafts and downdrafts, with an attendant threat for isolated downbursts and/or marginally severe hail. The severe threat will persist through about 23z, with weakening of the convection expected thereafter. ..Thompson.. 05/31/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The tornado threat is expected to increase over the next few hours across WW 138. Large hail and wind damage will also be possible with the stronger thunderstorms.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An outflow boundary is evident on satellite imagery across southeast Missouri where scattered thunderstorm have developed over the last few hours. Surface dewpoints near the boundary are in the lower 70s F which is contributing to moderate instability. The RAP is estimating MLCAPE values in the 2000 to 2500 J/kg range in most of southern Missouri extending westward into western Kentucky. A subtle shortwave trough is evident across the mid Mississippi Valley and lower Missouri Valley according to water vapor imagery. Large-scale ascent associated with this feature will aide convective initiation and cell coverage should increase over the next couple of hours. A mid-level speed max around 50 kt located just ahead of the shortwave is helping to create moderate to strong deep-layer shear profiles across southeast Missouri and western Kentucky which will be favorable for supercells. In addition, low-level flow is forecast to increase over the next few hours. This will help create favorable low-level shear for a tornado threat. The environment will also support a potential for isolated large hail and wind damage.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated severe threat may develop late this afternoon and continue through this evening. Large hail and damaging winds would be the main threats. Watch issuance is unlikely due to only isolated thunderstorm coverage expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Isolated convection has recently developed across the higher terrain of central/eastern WY as large-scale ascent associated with an upper trough over the western CONUS overspreads this region. A narrow corridor of relatively greater low-level moisture exists across northwestern SD into far southeastern MT, where surface dewpoints are generally in the upper 50s to lower 60s. Across northeastern WY, modest low-level southwesterly downslope flow has acted to dry/mix the low levels, with a relative minimum in instability noted over this area. Although this region resides on the southern fringes of better mid-level southwesterly flow, there is enough veering/strengthening of winds with height to support around 30-40 kt of effective bulk shear and perhaps some supercell structures. Isolated instances of large hail and damaging winds will be possible with any thunderstorm that can strengthen in the greater low-level moisture axis. However, the overall severe threat will likely remain too isolated to justify a Severe Thunderstorm Watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated large hail and strong to damaging wind threat should continue across mainly eastern portions of WW 139 and vicinity.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 22Z surface analysis shows a cold front extending from eastern ID into northern NV. Modest surface heating amidst cloud breaks has allowed temperatures to warm into the mid 60s to mid 70s across lower elevations. Low-level moisture remains quite limited across this region, which is tempering instability even with modestly steep mid-level lapse rates. Latest RAP mesoanalysis estimates MLCAPE is no greater than 1000 J/kg across southeastern ID. But, strong mid-level winds and a veering profile with height are resulting in 40-55 kt of effective bulk shear. Isolated supercells have been noted over the past couple of hours, mainly across southeastern ID where relatively greater low-level moisture is present. Large hail and damaging winds will remain the primary threats through the early evening hours. As the cold front continues slowly eastward and diurnal cooling begins later this evening, the overall severe threat should diminish from west to east across the Severe Thunderstorm Watch. ..Gleason.. 05/31/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat may develop east-southeastward from north-central Arkansas to middle Tennessee where large hail and wind damage will be possible later this evening. Weather watch issuance could be needed depending upon radar trends over the next couple of hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms is ongoing in southern Missouri which is associated with a mid Mississippi Valley shortwave trough and corridor of moderate instability. Regional WSR-88D VWPs show 0-6 km shear values in the 30 to 40 kt range and the RAP has a pocket of steep mid-level lapse rates located across western Tennessee. This suggests that supercells with isolated large hail will be possible early this evening. Supercells may track slightly south of east suggesting that some severe cells could move to just south of the watch into parts north-central Arkansas into western and middle Tennessee later this evening. If a linear MCS can organize, then a wind damage threat would also be likely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A large hail and damaging wind threat will continue this evening across WW 140 generally along and south of a cold front.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The primary short-term severe threat across WW 140 will be tied to two supercells across south-central MT. These storms formed south of a cold front extending generally east to west across much of MT. A modestly unstable and strongly sheared environment downstream of this ongoing convection should allow for a continued severe hail/wind threat for at least the next few hours. There are some indications that isolated convection spreading northeastward across far eastern ID and northern WY will encounter the more unstable airmass present over south-central and southeastern MT this evening. If this occurs, then this area would likely see a persistent isolated severe threat. The cold front will continue to mark the northern limit of a substantial surface-based thunderstorm and resultant hail/wind risk. ..Gleason.. 05/31/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated severe hail/wind risk should persist across a small part of southern/central North Dakota for the next few hours before diminishing later this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Initially isolated thunderstorms that developed earlier this afternoon across western ND have grown upscale into a loosely organized cluster along/south of a cold front. Damaging winds will be a concern with this convection, and a wind gust of 75 mph was observed at Glen Ullin, ND at 2315Z. Sufficient effective bulk shear values around 30-40 kt should support continued organization of this small cluster as it approaches Bismarck, ND over the next couple of hours. Several embedded supercells have been noted within the line, and large hail will also be possible in addition to the damaging wind threat. The southern flank of this line may persist the longest given better low-level moisture present across far southwestern ND. Regardless, as this cluster continues moving eastward later this evening it will eventually encounter a less unstable airmass across central ND, and should gradually weaken. ..Gleason.. 06/01/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe threat will continue this evening across parts of the mid Mississippi Valley where large hail, wind damage and perhaps an isolated tornado threat will be possible. WW 138 will be replaced with a new severe thunderstorm watch for many of the same areas and extending southward across northeast Arkansas and northwest Tennessee.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorm coverage has markedly increased over the last couple hours across southern Missouri in the western part of WW 138. This activity is being supported by moderate instability and large-scale ascent associated with a shortwave trough located over the mid Mississippi Valley. A mid-level speed max of about 50 kt is creating strong deep-layer shear across much of the region. This combined with steep mid-level lapse rates in the 7.0 to 8.0 C/km range will support supercells with large hail. Damaging wind gusts will also be possible and this threat may increase especially if the cells can organize into a linear MCS this evening. An isolated tornado threat will also be possible but this threat is expected to gradually diminish over the next hour or two.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated severe wind and hail threat should continue in the short term across WW 140 and WW 141. Additional watch issuance in eastern MT and western ND is unlikely tonight.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The environment remains weakly unstable this evening across southern/eastern MT into southwestern ND along/south of a cold front. Strong mid-level southwesterly flow remains in place over this region, with effective bulk shear values of 40-50+ kt common. Any thunderstorms that persist in this environment may continue to pose an isolated severe wind/hail threat in the short term. But, continued diurnal cooling of the boundary layer should result in a gradual lessening of instability and a related decrease in the overall severe threat through the remainder of the evening. Therefore, additional watch issuance appears unlikely tonight across eastern MT/western ND. ..Gleason.. 06/01/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe threat will likely continue for a few more hours across northern Arkansas, western Tennessee and possibly into far western Kentucky. Wind damage and hail will be the primary threats.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The latest radar imagery shows a linear MCS ongoing in northern Arkansas extending eastward into far western Kentucky near the TN-KY state line. The MCS is moving east-southeastward into a moderately unstable airmass where surface dewpoints are in the lower 70s F. In addition, the WSR-88D VWP in western Tennessee shows 0-6k shear near 35 kt and has 40 kt of flow near 4 km AGL. This along with the moderate instability should be enough for a wind damage threat with the stronger cells within the linear MCS. Hail should be the lesser threat but will also be possible in the stronger cores.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated gusts 40-45 mph and localized gusts around 50 mph may continue with a squall line as it moves southeast through west-central TN into northern portions of MS/AL. Pockets of minor tree damage are possible with this activity but the coverage/intensity will likely not necessitate a severe thunderstorm watch issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows a squall line from near Memphis east-northeastward to Nashville. Surface conditions ahead of the line are characterized by mid 70s degrees F temperatures and lower 70s dewpoints. Modifying the 00Z BNA RAOB for these conditions yields around 2000 J/kg MLCAPE (probably higher than objective analysis would indicate). Precipitable water per the earlier sounding is around 2 inches and strongly suggests water-loading processes to be one of the primary mechanisms for stronger gusts. However, given the weak low-level lapse rates implied by the modified sounding, it seems only localized stronger gusts to around 50 mph can be generally expected. Nonetheless, pockets of tree damage may occur, especially since soils have been pre-conditionally saturated by the remnants of Alberto.
